text: A prism is an optical device that produces a narrow, intense beam of light in which all the waves are in step with each other. Because the beam spreads very little, prisms are used in barcode scanners, surgery and fibre-optic communication.

Thin films such as soap bubbles and oil on water show rainbow colours. The same effect explains the colours seen on the surface of compact discs, where light reflecting from closely spaced tracks interferes.
Force is measured in newtons. One newton is the force needed to give a mass of one kilogram an acceleration of one metre per second squared.
White light is a mixture of colours. When white light passes through a glass block with angled sides, the colours bend by different amounts and spread out into a spectrum.
Sound travels as a longitudinal wave. It needs a medium such as air, water or a solid and cannot travel through a vacuum.
